title: The Simpleton and the Sharper
logline: A trickster swaps himself for a donkey on its lead rope, then tells the trusting owner he was a man cursed into donkey shape. The owner believes him so completely that when he later finds his own donkey for sale, he scolds it for sinning again and refuses to buy it.
moral: A man who believes everything he is told can be robbed twice: once of his donkey and once of his good sense.
tone: Deadpan comic folk tale. The humour comes from the gap between what the audience sees (two grinning thieves, a perfectly ordinary donkey) and what the gentle, sincere owner believes. He is never mocked cruelly; the donkey is the quiet witness.

beats.summary: A trusting man leads his donkey by a neck rope and never looks back.
The sharper bets his partner he can take the donkey behind the owner's back.
He unties the walking donkey while keeping the rope taut; the partner leads it away.
He puts the loop round his own neck and walks as the donkey.
He stops; the owner pulls and nothing moves.
The owner turns and finds a man where his donkey was.
The lie: a mother's curse turned him into a donkey.
And today her blessing turned him back: ta-da.
The owner believes, apologises and frees the thief.
His wife believes too and gives charity for forgiveness.
At the market he recognises his own donkey for sale.
He scolds the donkey for beating its mother again and refuses to buy it.
He walks away proud, never understanding he was tricked.

props.description: Planned asset 'rope (lead)': a rope from a hand to a neck loop. leadRope(ctx, [hx, hy], [nx, ny], {slack 0..1, loop: 'on' | 'off' | 'open', r, vib}). Rope 7 px brown line with black brush outline, length 190 world units at rest; slack 1 = sagging catenary (mid point 40 below the chord), slack 0 = dead straight, vib adds a 3 px sine shiver. The loop is an ellipse 46 x 30 around the neck (drawn in two halves, behind and in front of the neck) with a small knot; 'open' is the loop held in two hands (ellipse 70 x 50); 'off' ends in the empty loop lying on the ground. Also a coiled state on the floor (3 turns, radius 30) and a hung state on a peg.
packLoad(ctx, ['sack', 'sack'], x, y, s): the donkey's sack (via the donkey load field) and the two sacks the simpleton carries on his own back in S13.

The sharper's told story, staged inside the Library thoughtCloud (w 720, h 420, centred near world y 330, tail to the sharper's head, scale 0.5, at [500, 760]). Same cloud for the wife's worry (smaller: w 420, h 280, scale 0.34) and the simpleton's 'where is my donkey' (w 300, h 220).
Planned asset wineCup: small stemmed cup 30 x 44 held in the hand, tilt and two spilling red drops; also used as a flat icon in the balloon.
Planned asset purse: fat yellow coin purse 44 x 52 with a red tie; jingle = 2 px bounce with two small accent lines. Single coins (planned coinPile coin: yellow disc r 9, black outline) fly from it.
Planned asset smallBowl: brown half-ellipse bowl 50 x 22 held by the beggar; coins land in it.

subtitles.ar: كان رجل ساذج يمشي في الطريق،|ويجر حماره خلفه بحبل مربوط إلى عنقه.|رآه محتالان، فقال أحدهما لصاحبه|إنه يستطيع أخذ الحمار دون أن يشعر صاحبه بما يجري خلف ظهره.
subtitles.en: A simple man walked along|leading his donkey by a rope.|Two tricksters saw him, and one promised his partner|he could steal the animal without its owner noticing.

subtitles.ar: اقترب المحتال الأول بهدوء،|وفك الحبل من عنق الحمار،|ثم سلمه إلى صاحبه ليبتعد به.|وبعد ذلك وضع الحبل حول عنقه هو، ومشى خلف الرجل كأنه الحمار الذي كان يقوده.
subtitles.en: One trickster quietly unfastened the donkey|and gave it to his partner.|He looped the rope around his own neck|and followed the unsuspecting man.

subtitles.ar: ظل الرجل يمشي زمنًا دون أن يلتفت،|حتى توقف المحتال عن الحركة.|شد الرجل الحبل، فلم يتحرك شيء.|التفت أخيرًا، فوجد رجلًا مكان حماره، فصاح من شدة الدهشة وسأله ماذا حدث.
subtitles.en: The man kept walking|until the trickster stopped.|Pulling the rope did nothing.|When he turned, he saw a man where his donkey should have been and demanded an explanation.

subtitles.ar: قال المحتال إنه كان إنسانًا،|لكنه عاد إلى بيته يومًا وهو سكران، وضرب أمه عندما نصحته بالتوبة.|فدعت عليه، وتحول بسبب دعائها إلى حمار،|وعاش على هذه الصورة سنوات.
subtitles.en: The trickster claimed he had once been human|but beat his mother while drunk.|Her curse had turned him into a donkey,|he said, for many years.

subtitles.ar: وأضاف أن أمه تذكرت ابنها اليوم، فدعت له بالخير،|وعاد فورًا إلى صورته البشرية.|صدق الرجل القصة، واعتذر لأنه كان يركبه ويحمله الأثقال،|ثم فك الحبل وترك المحتال يذهب.
subtitles.en: He said his mother had finally forgiven him,|restoring his human form.|The simpleton believed the tale, apologized for riding him,|and released the thief.

subtitles.ar: رجع إلى بيته حزينًا، وقص على زوجته ما اعتقد أنه حدث.|صدقته هي أيضًا، وخافت أن يكونا قد ظلما رجلًا دون علمهما،|فتصدقت بشيء من المال طلبًا للمغفرة.
subtitles.en: At home he told his wife the extraordinary story.|She believed him too|and gave charity, fearing they had unknowingly mistreated a human being.

subtitles.ar: بعد أيام قالت الزوجة إن البيت يحتاج إلى حمار يعمل به زوجها،|فذهب إلى السوق ليشتري واحدًا.|وبين الحيوانات المعروضة رأى حماره القديم نفسه،|فعرف شكله وصوته دون أي شك.
subtitles.en: Days later his wife asked him|to buy another working donkey.|At the market he recognized his own animal|among those offered for sale.

subtitles.ar: اقترب الرجل من أذن الحمار وهمس غاضبًا:|يبدو أنك عدت إلى السكر وضرب أمك مرة ثانية،|لكنني لن أشتريك بعد اليوم!|ثم تركه ومضى، ولم يفهم أنه وقع في خدعة اللصوص.
subtitles.en: The man whispered angrily to the donkey|that it must have beaten its mother again.|He refused to buy it,|never realizing the tricksters had fooled him.

new_assets.name: rope (lead)
new_assets.description: leadRope: the planned lead rope between a hand and a neck loop, here the central prop of the film. States: on an animal neck, opened in two hands, on a person's neck, taut with vibration, dragged on the floor, coiled, tied to a post.
new_assets.implementation: leadRope(ctx, a, b, {slack, loop, r, vib, t}): quadratic curve from a to b with the control point at the midpoint lowered by 40 * slack (plus 3 * vib * sin(40 t)); stroke 11 px black then 7 px brown. Loop = ellipse (46 x 30 on the donkey, 40 x 22 on a person) drawn as a back half before the neck and a front half after it, knot = 8 px disc. 'open' = ellipse 70 x 50 between two hand points. Coil = 3 concentric ellipses radius 30, 22, 14. Length kept near 190 by placing the follower at SX - 190.

new_assets.name: poofTransform
new_assets.description: Planned transformation burst (KD-014): stars spiral in, star burst and puff ring with a 2 frame flash, two black silhouettes cross scaled inside (from, to), puff clears. Used inside the tale cloud forward (man to donkey, 81.78) and reversed (donkey to man, 95.94).
new_assets.implementation: poofTransform(ctx, x, y, t, t0, {from(c), to(c), dur: 1.3, r: 150}): 0-35 %: 8 yellow 5 point stars on a shrinking spiral; 35-45 %: white flash 2 frames + 12 point burst polygon (yellow, red dot fill) scaling 0.2 to 1.1; 35-70 %: from() drawn with silhouette: true scaling 1 to 0.6 while to() scales 0.6 to 1; 60-100 %: ring of 9 puff circles expanding and fading. Pure function of t.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the supplied English is a condensed summary, not a line by line translation (it omits, among others, the rope tied to the donkey's neck, 'walked behind him as if he were the donkey', the mother's advice to repent, 'and loaded him with burdens', 'knew its shape and its voice', and the direct speech 'I will not buy you after today'); both texts are kept verbatim and the subtitle chunks are aligned as closely as the two allow.
Violence softened: the son striking his mother (76.32) is shown only inside the tale cloud and is hidden by a star burst with BAM!, with no contact drawn; default kept.

Drinking is shown inside the tale cloud with a small wine cup, a zigzag walk, spiral eyes and HIC! (72-76 s) and as a wine cup icon in the whisper balloon (162 s); default kept, alternative is the zigzag walk only.
Addition beyond the script: the two tricksters are shown as the sellers at the market, hiding behind a hay bale and peeking out at the end to make 'the thieves' trick' visible; default kept.
Addition beyond the script: the charity (127.76-131.2) is shown as coins given to a poor old man at the door; default kept.

Invented English lettering: title, SHHH!, TUG!, TUUUG!, WHAAAT?!, HIC!, BAM!, POOF! (twice), TA-DA!, CLINK!, OOF!, HEE HAW!, NO SALE!, HEE HEE!, THE END, plus labels HIS DONKEY, THE NEW DONKEY, ME A MAN, HUMAN AGAIN!, THE MARKET, THE SAME DONKEY!, counters MILES and YEARS, card DAYS LATER...; default kept.
The donkey's identifying mark is a red bridle (Library bridle field) so that he reads as the same animal at the market; default kept.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template. One position function drives the whole road section: SX(t) = 80 + 45 t until 49.3, then fixed at 2298; follower (donkey, then sharper) at SX - 190. Use walk() on both so no foot slides; camera x derives from SX.

The Library person is front facing only. 'Not looking back' is carried by gaze [1, 0] plus body lean toward the walking direction; the turn at 57.06 uses a turnFlip style squeeze and a gaze flip to [-1, 0]. Keep the simpleton's gaze strictly forward from 0 to 55.9 except the fly beat at 46.18.
